author: agentA induced (sandboxed) from bundle 0001950803.json; StepStone pipe-delimited floating senior-secured-loan dialect

applies_to.note: Dominant rate-bearing variant under the per-CIK anchors (7332 rows, 89.1% of the CIK). Pipe-delimited: '<affil> | <secured type> | <industry> | <issuer+instrument> | <REF token: [tenor] REF + <spread>%[ / <floor>%]> | <rate token: <all-in>%[ / <pik>%]> | <m/d/y>'. Rate token 1 carries the reference index (e.g. '3M SOFR'), the credit SPREAD (first %), and an optional rate FLOOR (second %). Rate token 2 carries the ALL-IN coupon (first %) and an optional PIK rate (second %). SPREAD/RATE ARE PERCENT (5.50% -> 0.055), NOT bps -- twins confirm (basis_spread 0.055 for '5.50%'). The reference index VALUE is not printed; the all-in coupon is printed verbatim and gated against the interest_rate twin.

_pik_convention_doc: ADDITIVE. The all-in 'interest_rate' twin equals the printed first % of rate token 2, which itself equals reference+spread (the cash/floating coupon), with PIK shown SEPARATELY as the second % of token 2. Direct evidence: Echo Purchaser Term Loan '3M SOFR + 5.50% /0.75% | 10.83% /3.50%' -- 3M SOFR at 2024-03-31 (~5.33%) + spread 5.50% = 10.83% = the printed all-in EXACTLY, while PIK 3.50% is a separate component NOT included in the 10.83. Corroborated by AMEX Holding '3M SOFR + 6.65% | 11.96%' (5.30 + 6.65 = 11.95 ~ 11.96). Therefore the printed interest_rate is the cash leg and PIK accrues ON TOP (additive), not inclusive. No self-contained 'X cash plus Y PIK = Z total' is printed (the reference value is absent), so sum_identity is NOT applicable; gating is against the reliable structured twins. NOTE the data also contains degenerate token-2 values like '1.00%' or '0.50%' where the all-in collapses to the floor/spread artifact (e.g. spread '+1.00%'); those are real filer data quirks, flagged via the twin invariant, not fit around.

extractors._doc: ALL-IN coupon = the rate field IMMEDIATELY before the maturity date (m/d/yyyy or mm-dd-yyyy). FIX (Agent A2). Prior regex grabbed the FIRST numeric field after the spread and closed on any '|<digit>', so it (a) captured the standalone PIK-spread field in the EXTRA-FIELD layout '... | 0.75% | 11.33% | DATE' (wrong -> 0.75) and (b) had no date anchor. This regex anchors the all-in to the LAST pipe field before a DATE via a date lookahead after the closing '|', so the EXTRA-FIELD standalone PIK pipe '| 0.75% |' is skipped and only '| 11.33% | DATE' matches -> 11.33. The captured value's '%' is OPTIONAL: StepStone prints the all-in three printed ways and all three with value >= 1 are already PERCENT scale, handled by engine 'pct' (float as-is): (1) PERCENT-FORM '14.14%/ 1.25%' -> 14.14; (2) EXTRA-FIELD '| 11.33% |' -> 11.33; (3) BARE-PERCENT (no '%' sign) '| 11.61 |' / '| 12.70/4.00% |' / '| 10.596 |' -> 11.61/12.70/10.596. The within-field PIK leg '/ x%' (with or without space, '14.14%/1.25%' or '12.70/4.00%') is absorbed and excluded. ENGINE CONSTRAINT: _coerce supports only pct/bps/date_mdy/ref_code/text -- there is NO multiply-by-100 / pct_or_decimal / auto type, and apply_grammar last-write-wins assigns None for a non-matching extractor (so a second decimal-only extractor for the same field would clobber percent-form rows with None). The BARE-DECIMAL-FRACTION layout '... |0.1111 | DATE' (= 11.11%, ~28 rows; bare value < 1 meaning a fraction that must be *100) CANNOT be rescaled by any supported coercion, so those ~28 rows match here and are read as-is (0.1111) which will MISS the twin (na/fail) -- recovering them requires an engine 'pct_or_decimal' coercion (abs<1 -> *100), an engine change that is OUT OF SCOPE for a grammar-only repair. NOTE: bare values < 1 that are genuine low coupons in percent scale (e.g. '| 0.50 | DATE', twin 0.5) DO match correctly as-is.
